extracted.intended_audience: poets and writers seeking prescriptive guidance on composing short lyric/ narrative poems
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive method for composing a short, unified poem (one-sitting lyric/narrative) that produces a single vivid poetic effect; covers planning, tone, refrain, versification, and devices to build suggestiveness and dénouement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elaborate the dénouement before writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing is more clear than that every plot, worth the name, must be elaborated to its dénouement before anything be attempted with the pen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan the ending (climax, final query, or dénouement) first so all incidents and tone can be made to tend toward that intention. Poe says the poem 'may be said to have its beginning—at the end,' and composes the climactic stanza early to guide preceding material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commence with a single effect
rubrics_metrics.description: I prefer commencing with the consideration of an effect... Having chosen a novel, first, and secondly a vivid effect, I consider whether it can be best wrought by incident or tone...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide on one novel, vivid impression you want the reader to experience; build every choice (tone, incident, meter) to produce that single effect rather than multiple competing aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep originality always in view
rubrics_metrics.description: Keeping originality always in view—for he is false to himself who ventures to dispense with so obvious and so easily attainable a source of interest...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberately seek originality (often by negation and careful effort rather than impulse). Avoid cliché solutions; originality can be achieved through novel combinations of familiar elements (e.g., Poe's combination of meter/stanza).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decide whether effect is by incident, tone, or both
rubrics_metrics.description: I consider whether it can be best wrought by incident or tone—whether by ordinary incidents and peculiar tone, or the converse, or by peculiarity both of incident and tone...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly choose the balance of plot/events vs. tonal, atmospheric writing to achieve your intended effect and select devices accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit length to preserve unity of impression (single sitting)
rubrics_metrics.description: If any literary work is too long to be read at one sitting, we must be content to dispense with the immensely important effect derivable from unity of impression... there is a distinct limit, as regards length, to all works of literary art—the limit of a single sitting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep a poem short enough to be read in one sitting so the intended effect remains unified. Poe determined ~100 lines for his target intensity; brevity should be in direct ratio to intended intensity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make Beauty the poem's primary province; subordinate Truth and Passion
rubrics_metrics.description: I say... that Beauty is the sole legitimate province of the poem... Truth... and Passion... are, although attainable..., far more readily attainable in prose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize aesthetic elevation/beauty as the dominant objective; if introducing passion or truth, tone them into subservience to the predominant aim so they serve the overall poetic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select a single, predominant tone (melancholy recommended)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regarding, then, Beauty as my province, my next question referred to the tone of its highest manifestation—and all experience has shown that this tone is one of sadness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a consistent tone (Poe favors melancholy for highest poetic effect) and ensure all elements—diction, incident, rhythm—support that tone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a refrain and diversify its application
rubrics_metrics.description: I determined to produce continuously novel effects, by the variation of the application of the refrain—the refrain itself remaining, for the most part, unvaried.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ a recurring refrain (burden) whose repetition yields increasing effects by changing context/implication each time rather than by monotonous identical use; keep the refrain text largely unchanged while varying its application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep the refrain brief—ideally a single word
rubrics_metrics.description: In proportion to the brevity of the sentence, would, of course, be the facility of the variation. This led me at once to a single word as the best refrain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a very short refrain (a word or short phrase) to make it easier to vary its implications stanza to stanza and to allow prolonged emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose a sonorous refrain consonant with tone
rubrics_metrics.description: That such a close, to have force, must be sonorous and susceptible of protracted emphasis... these considerations inevitably led me to the long 'o' as the most sonorous vowel, in connection with 'r' as the most producible consonant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select sounds and phonemes (vowels/consonants) that permit protracted emphasis and fit the poem's tone; Poe's 'Nevermore' chosen for long 'o' + 'r' illustrates aligning sound to effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the speaker plausibly capable of repeating the refrain (use non-reasoning creature if needed)
rubrics_metrics.description: I did not fail to perceive, in short, that the difficulty lay in the reconciliation of this monotony with the exercise of reason on the part of the creature repeating the word. Here... arose the idea of a non-reasoning creature capable of speech...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the repeated refrain would be unreasonable for a human speaker, choose a narrator/character (e.g., a bird, automaton) whose behavior plausibly explains repetition without logical contradiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish the climax stanza first to fix rhythm and stakes
rubrics_metrics.description: I composed this stanza, at this point, first that, by establishing the climax, I might the better vary and graduate...and...definitely settle the rhythm, the meter, and the length and general arrangement of the stanza...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write the climactic stanza early to set the metric/rhythmic benchmark and to guide the grading of seriousness and importance in preceding stanzas; avoid later stanzas accidentally exceeding climactic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure subsequent stanzas do not surpass the climactic stanza in effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Had I been able, in the subsequent composition, to construct more vigorous stanzas, I should, without scruple, have purposely enfeebled them, so as not to interfere with the climacteric effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control the vigor of stanzas to preserve the climax's primacy—intentionally weaken otherwise stronger passages if they would undermine the climax.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek originality in versification through novel combinations
rubrics_metrics.description: The possible varieties of meter and stanza are absolutely infinite... originality (unless in minds of very unusual force) is by no means a matter...to be found, it must be elaborately sought...what originality 'The Raven' has, is in their combination into stanza.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Innovate not necessarily in each metrical foot but in the novel combination of meters, stanza-lengths, rhyme, and alliteration. Deliberate design can yield original rhythmic effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose meter and stanza deliberately to support rhythm and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: My first object (as usual) was originality... The former is trochaic—the latter is octameter acatalectic, alternating with heptameter catalectic repeated in the refrain... terminating with tetrameter catalectic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select specific metrical patterns and stanzaic architecture that reinforce the poem's mood and allow the intended musical and emphatic moments; set the rhythmical standard with the climax stanza.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a circumscribed locale to concentrate attention
rubrics_metrics.description: It has always appeared to me that a close circumscription of space is absolutely necessary to the effect of insulated incident: it has the force of a frame to a picture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the action in a confined, well-characterized setting (e.g., a chamber) to focus the reader's attention and enhance the unity and intensity of the effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design incidents to prolong curiosity and create contrasts
rubrics_metrics.description: The idea of making the lover suppose... that the flapping of the wings of the bird against the shutter is a 'tapping' at the door, originated in a wish to increase, by prolonging, the reader’s curiosity...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange events (tapping, tempest, shutters) to sustain suspense, justify character actions, and create contrasts (outside tempest vs interior serenity) that heighten the central effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ contrast (comic/fantastic vs grave; marble vs plumage; storm vs interior)
rubrics_metrics.description: The effect of this originality of combination is aided by other unusual and some altogether novel effects, arising from an extension of the application of the principles of rhyme and alliteration... I have availed myself of the force of contrast...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use contrasts—textural, tonal, or visual (bust of Pallas vs raven plumage; ludicrous entrance vs subsequent solemnity)—to deepen the ultimate impression and prepare shifts in feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition from fantastic to profound seriousness at the right moment
rubrics_metrics.description: The effect of the dénouement being thus provided for, I immediately drop the fantastic for a tone of the most profound seriousness—this tone commencing in the stanza directly following...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time tonal shifts carefully: introduce a lighter or fantastic element early to engage, then decisively shift to seriousness to lead into the dénouement and intensify emotional impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add complexity and an under-current of suggestiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Two things are invariably required: first, some amount of complexity, or, more properly, adaptation; and, secondly, some amount of suggestiveness—some under-current, however indefinite, of meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond the overt narrative, plant ambiguous or symbolic elements that invite interpretation and give richness; allow suggestiveness to pervade earlier narrative so later emblematic meaning feels earned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce metaphorical language to signal emblematic meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: It will be observed that the words, 'from out my heart,' involve the first metaphorical expression in the poem... They... dispose the mind to seek a moral in all that has been previously narrated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a carefully placed metaphor or figurative phrase to pivot the reader from literal reading to emblematic/symbolic interpretation, enabling a deeper final resonance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground the initial narrative in plausible, accountable reality before symbolic overlay
rubrics_metrics.description: So far, everything is within the limits of the accountable—of the real... The student now guesses the state of the case, but is impelled...to propound such queries...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First present events with plausible, real-world explanations (a bird learned a word, a storm forced it in) so that subsequent symbolic or supernatural readings gain power through contrast with earlier plausibility.
